{{Quote|Your Padawan isn't who you think. She's no Jedi. She's a Child of the Emperor, like me. And it's time she returned to our father's warm embrace.|Valis|<ref name="The Defector" />}}
During the [[Desolator crisis]] of [[3643 BBY]], the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Valis]] lured the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Kira Carsen]] and her [[Hero of Tython|master]] to an [[Czerka asteroid mining facility|abandoned mining facility]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]], forcing a '''duel''' between them. Valis was a [[Children of the Emperor|Child of the Emperor]]&mdash;an agent of the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor's]] will&mdash;and, on the orders of his "father," sought to bring the former Child Carsen back into the fold. Believing that they were meeting [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Hacklin]] of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] to negotiate his defection, Carsen and her [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] teacher traveled to the station, but instead found Valis, and he was [[Death/Legends|killed]] in the fight that followed. As a result of the [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]], Carsen revealed her past to both her master and the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]], giving the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] concrete evidence about the existence of the Children.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|One of Darth Angral's closest advisors&mdash;Admiral Hacklin&mdash;asked us for asylum. He wants to defect.|General Var Suthra|<ref name="The Defector" />}}
[[Kira Carsen]] was born on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]], the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], and given as an infant to the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]] on the planet [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. As a child, she was selected by the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]] to become one of his [[Children of the Emperor|Children]]&mdash;agents of his will who unknowingly served as his [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and [[Ear/Legends|ears]] throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. However, Carsen fled the Empire before the process could be completed, leaving behind her fellow Children such as [[Valis]]<ref name="The Defector" /> and [[Suri]].<ref name="Orphans">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|The Emperor's Orphans|Voss}}</ref> She made her way to the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] and lived on the streets before becoming a member of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], though she hid her past and her Imperial heritage out of fear of being kicked out.<ref name="The Defector" />

In [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="Time" /> the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Angral]] [[Desolator crisis|declared war]] on the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the Jedi Order in response to his son [[Tarnis (Sith Lord)|Tarnis's]] [[Death/Legends|death]] [[Duel in the Jedi Temple ruins|at the hands]] of Carsen and a [[Hero of Tython|young Jedi Knight]]. Angral seized control of several Republic [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]], prompting the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] and Carsen to pursue Angral's agents across the galaxy, and the Knight took on Carsen as a Padawan, as Carsen's previous Master [[Bela Kiwiiks]] was on her own assignment. While the Knight was on a [[Mission to Ord Mantell|mission]] to the surface of [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]], Carsen remained behind on the [[Ord Mantell Orbital Station]], where an Imperial operative identified her as the Knight's apprentice and contacted Darth Angral. Angral and his retainers,<ref name="New Intelligence">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|New Intelligence|Ord Mantell}}</ref> including [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Hacklin]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]],<ref name="The Defector" /> arrived and interrogated Carsen as to the Knight's whereabouts, though Carsen tricked the Sith Lord into heading to the planet [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]].<ref name="New Intelligence" /> Though Carsen escaped Angral's [[Ferav|servants]] with the help of her teacher, Angral recognized her as a former Child, and the knowledge of her survival reached the Emperor.<ref name="The Defector" />

==The duel==
{{Quote|Accept the truth, sister. You belong to the Emperor&mdash;and our father will have you back.''"<br />"''No. I'll die first.''"<br />"''So be it&mdash;sister. Then I must kill you and your Master.|Valis and Kira Carsen|<ref name="The Defector" />}}
[[File:Valis_fight.png|thumb|right|250px|Valis repels Carsen's initial attack.]]
Determined to recapture Carsen, the Emperor dispatched his Child Valis to bring her back to him. Posing as Admiral Hacklin, Valis contacted the Republic and claimed that he wanted to defect&mdash;but would only do so to Carsen and her master. [[General/Legends|General]] [[Var Suthra]] arranged for a meeting between "Hacklin" and the two Jedi at an [[Czerka asteroid mining facility|abandoned mining facility]] formerly operated by [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Corporation]] in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. Valis arrived before the Jedi, and he departed his ship and hid among the cargo crates within the facility's hangar. When the two Jedi arrived, he watched them approach his ship before stepping out into the light and speaking to them. After introducing himself and thanking the pair for coming, Valis apologized for the deception, but Carsen immediately recognized him and warned her Master to attack. Amused, Valis explained that Carsen was of the Empire and a Child of the Emperor like him, and that their father desired his wayward Child returned to him.<ref name="The Defector" />

The Knight refused Valis's request that the Jedi allow him to take Carsen home, and the Padawan charged the Sith and brought her [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsaber]] down upon his head&mdash;only for Valis to summon his own lightsaber to his hands and block the attack before [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinetically]] blasting her backwards. The Knight rushed to Carsen's defense, and battle was joined between the three combatants. Despite Valis's combat prowess and skill with both telekinesis and [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], the Child was ultimately no match for the combined strength of Carsen and the Jedi Knight, and he was slain.<ref name="The Defector" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|I'm ready to tell the truth&mdash;Master Kiwiiks, the Jedi Council, everyone. No more secrets.|Kira Carsen|<ref name="The Defector" />}}
Once the two Jedi returned to their [[Hero of Tython's Defender-class light corvette|ship]], Carsen revealed her past to her teacher, and the Knight and Carsen revealed her past to the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] as well. Despite Master [[Jaric Kaedan]]'s desire to banish her from the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Satele Shan]] gave her blessing for Carsen to continue as the Knight's apprentice, though General Suthra was wary of her involvement in further operations.<ref name="The Defector" /> When the conflict with Angral came to a head in a [[Battle of the Oppressor|battle]] over the planet [[Tython/Legends|Tython]], Angral was slain by the Knight, but the Emperor reached out to his former Child and took complete possession of her. However, with her teacher's help, Carsen was able to drive out the Emperor and sever the link between them.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Fate of the Jedi|the ''Oppressor''}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The duel with Valis first appeared in the Jedi Knight class mission "The Defector" in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a [[Star Wars video games|video game]] released in [[2011]]. The mission serves as the intermission of the Act I story, bridging the class storylines on the moon Nar Shaddaa and the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="The Defector" />
